ORDER BY clause qualification broken after recent changes

#### Description

The ORDER BY clause qualification is not working correctly. When qualifying columns in queries with ORDER BY, the ordering expressions are not being properly handled, causing incorrect SQL generation.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import sqlglot
from sqlglot import optimizer

# Simple ORDER BY case
sql = "SELECT a FROM table1 ORDER BY a"
parsed = sqlglot.parse_one(sql)
qualified = optimizer.qualify_columns.qualify_columns(parsed, schema={}, infer_schema=False)
print(qualified.sql())
# Expected: SELECT table1.a AS a FROM table1 ORDER BY table1.a
# Actual: Incorrect output

# More complex case with positional reference
sql = "SELECT a, b FROM table1 ORDER BY 1"
parsed = sqlglot.parse_one(sql)
qualified = optimizer.qualify_columns.qualify_columns(parsed, schema={}, infer_schema=False)
print(qualified.sql())
# Expected: SELECT table1.a AS a, table1.b AS b FROM table1 ORDER BY table1.a
# Actual: Incorrect output
```

The issue appears to affect various ORDER BY scenarios including positional references and column names. This breaks SQL optimization and qualification functionality.
